recipes.name: Hot Bean Dip
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package shredded Monterey Jack cheese

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix cream cheese and sour cream together in a medium bowl until well blended.
Mix in refried beans, 1/2 of the Cheddar cheese, 1/2 of the Monterey Jack cheese, green onions, parsley, taco seasoning, and hot pepper sauce until well combined.
Transfer mixture to an 8x12-inch baking dish and sprinkle remaining Cheddar and Monterey Jack over the top.
Bake in the preheated oven until dip is hot and bubbly and cheese is golden brown, 20 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Hot Bean Dip
raw_recipe.description: This warm bean dip, made with refried beans, spices, and lots of cheese, is ready in 30 minutes and is always a crowd-pleaser at any gathering.

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipe. I have made this many times. You will need the whole package of taco seasoning for more flavor, get mild and it won't be hot. Make sure to soften the cream cheese in the microwave and stir the sour cream and cream cheese with the taco seasoning well before mixing in the refried beans. I double and make a 9x13 dish. Thanks.

Delicious! This makes a ton of dip though. You'd better be feeding a crowd or do what I did; Keep the topping cheese separate from the mixed dip and dish out about 8-16 oz (a dip size portion) into a small microwave dish. Heat the dip up then put an appropriate portion of the two cheese topping on the top. Cover for a couple of minutes to melt the cheese. Don't heat the dip up with the cheese on it. The cheese ends up all melting into the dip and disappearing. You can dish the refrigerated dip and cheese out for several nights as leftovers. Oh I used a whole package of the taco mix and used pepperjack cheese instead of the monterey. Otherwise I followed the recipe to a tee. Yummmy yummy!

I end up making it for dinner and I do browned hamburger with onion and Serrano peppers then do my own taco seasoning. I put the hamburger mixture on the bottom then the beans over the top. It's very very good.

I made it with SIETE Black Refried Beans (my favorite beans). Then, I browned a pound of ground beef, mixed an entire package of taco seasoning mix with the drained ground beef and proceeded with the rest of the recipe. We like it this way, because with tortilla chips, it makes it even heartier. More like a meal with drinks. You can choose from Mild taco seasoning mixes or Spicy. I went with the spicy, but it depends on your taste. The spicy can add a little heat to it.

Not sure the cream cheese or sour cream needed with the beans. I used to make this many years ago when unemployed. Layer beans, salsa, cheddar cheese in iron skillet and warm up on stove top, serve with corn chips. Great meal when on a budget. Three ingredients + chips. Buy the canned beans with seasoning added.

Things I changed or added: 
shredded chicken (boil a chicken breast for about 12 min then remove and use two forks to shred), one tomato chopped, garlic powder, onion powder, finely chopped white onion, FRESH parsley (dried is too bland), finely diced green chilies (found at Indian stores). I did measure cheese just added handfuls and did not add Frank's Red Hot because I added the hot chilies and I didn't add green onions. I also only used 1 can refried and the other can use whole cannellini beans

What we thought of dip: very tasty! Of course we added our own ingredients to tweak it but overall this recipe was a good backbone

Another recipe that's good as is , but also open to a variety of modifications. Myself, I add a half pound of ground beef and a half pound of ground pork. I put in my own mix of taco seasoning and a tablespoon of crushed red pepper. I make a tomatio, tomato, onion and jalapeno salsa ( fresh jalapenos). After I slow cook the beans and meat in the oven, I sprinkle a Spanish blend of shredded cheese on top. Finally I scoop on sour cream and serve with home made tortilla chips. I've served this in Mexico, Belize, Guatemala, Panema, Peru, Puerto Rico and Cuba. Spanish families from all of these areas seamed to like it quite well, so I might be doing something right

Love this recipe, but I never use a recipe as it so I love it for the ability to be versatile!! I didn't have monterey jack cheese or taco seasoning. For monterey substitute I used shredded mozzarella, and it was so good! Instead of taco seasoning I used garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder and a spicy blend I use in everything, and I used more hot sauce than recommended. To stop the cheese from getting crusty on top I added green chiles right on top before baking. The whole family loves it!

I make this often and it’s always loved.... I adlib when I don’t have all the ingredients on hand or... like the other day I wanted it in a hurry... When I’m in Mexico I’ll use the refried beans with the chorizo... and instead of taco seasoning will just add slightly drained canned salsa as well as tinned jalapeños (chopped fine) along with the onions, sour cream and cheeses... I also just popped it into the microwave to heat.. then taste test and adjust ...

We loved this! The is a hot version of 7 layer taco dip - for which there are many variations of, but this takes that concept and simplifies it - and says “hey! I’m even better heated through!” Which I think it is! I get why submitter and reviewers alike gain fans from non-bean-believers because this doesn’t taste like your typical bean dip! I used homemade taco seasoning and half a packet is 2 TBLS. Very good but next time I will up to 3. If you bake in a 2qt dish like I did, the bake time is almost double. Terrific appetizer or snack. Will go into hosting rotation! Thanks J Van Liere!

Very popular. I will definitely make it again. I cut the recipe in half and it was a good amount for 4-6 people as an appetizer. I added 1/2 of a small can of diced green chilies and 1 large clove of garlic, grated. I also used the full 1/4 cup of green onions plus a little more sprinkled on top after cooking. otherwise, I followed the recipe.
I'm definitely going to make this but I think I'm going to just make burritos out of it instead of a dip!
Made this for a potluck, came home with a clean baking dish and several asking for the recipe! Easy to make, budget friendly, and delicious!

Easy recipe to cut down, which I did. I also used more of the cheese in the dip vs on top and didn't cut the taco seasoning, probably added more. The constancy is like the canned bean dip, so if you like that, you'll love this.
I love it as is. My husband thought it was too hot so I just eliminate the hot sauce

This is the second time I've made this dip. This time, I used fresh beans instead of canned - let them simmer until squishy (4-6 hours altogether?) Also used half the cream cheese this time. I don't use taco seasoning- too much salt! - but I add all the other taco seasonings: cumin, paprika, chili powder, onion powder, garlic. This is a fantastic recipe, thank you!
Delicious and so easy to make.
i use cayenne instead hot sauce. we also use a little less sour cream and cream cheese;)

This was my first time making this recipe. My partner forgot to buy cream cheese, so I just added some more sour cream and cheese. Everyone at the family gathering said they loved it. I was asked to share the recipe. I'm excited to try it again with all the ingredients. I imagine it will be a smash at the next gathering.
I made some subs but it does make a lot so I used half to mix with plain pulled pork. I filled tortillas, rolled them and baked it with enchilada sauce. Queso fresco on top.
